correctness.rationale: The affine-barycentric halfspace criterion is exact for any tetrahedron. Three negative coordinates would place one sampled boundary point in the strict interior of K because it is a convex combination with positive weight at 0, impossible. Independent antipodal symmetry yields sixteen equally likely sign patterns of a one-dimensional null vector, and none are singular under the no-plane-mass assumptions. The 2+8+6 split exhausts cases; exact rational sign enumeration and independent facet tests corroborate every case. The common-boundary scope and no-three-negative boundary are stated.

originality.rationale: Wendel (1962) already gives the zero-visible mass in symmetric models. Bonnet–O'Reilly (2019/2022) gives signed-height expected facet counts for spherical i.i.d. uniform laws; these can recover the numerical spherical tetrahedron probabilities with Wendel and elementary convexity, so those numerical special cases are not the originality basis. The assessed claim is the full conditional 16-orientation classification and resulting full law simultaneously for all centered symmetric convex bodies and four arbitrary independent, potentially different antipodally invariant boundary distributions. The inspected literature and closest searches do not establish that stronger claim. Its full priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: There may be older unlocated work on visibility-complex face counts or signed simplex barycentric coordinates giving the same generalized law.

Uniform spherical numerical probabilities can be recovered from previously published expected negative-facet formulas plus Wendel and a geometric bound; only the stronger distribution-free nonidentical-boundary statement is claimed as a new contribution.
Finite exact sign configurations and simulations do not themselves prove universality; the proof relies on the conditional sign counting and convex-boundary lemma.

value.rationale: The theorem completes the stochastic visibility classification of a natural inscribed tetrahedron beyond the classical center-containment event, and proves robustness under all centered symmetric convex shapes and four arbitrary independent anisotropic antipodal measures. The deterministic boundary obstruction explains why the simple exact masses survive. A rational interior-point configuration shows the common-boundary assumption is sharp and needed; it is not a merely chosen coordinate sample or negative type check.
